chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Layth al-Muradi who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Cushions are in the house, containing statues/images on the right or left.' He said: 'There is no harm as long as they are not facing the Qiblah. If any of them are in front of you, facing the Qiblah, cover it and pray. If you have black dirhams (coins) with images on them, do not place them in front of you, but place them behind you.'

key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: The direction of prayer (towards the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ: In front of you (the direction faced during prayer)
key_terms.دَرَاهِمُ سُود: Black dirhams (ancient coins, often silver or gold, used here to represent currency with images)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in a room with statues or images?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *kiswa al-qiblah* (covering images) by distinguishing between lateral placement, which is permissible, and frontal placement, which requires covering or moving the object. It extends the principle of avoiding visual distraction or reverence to currency (*dirhams*), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining spiritual focus during prayer. The ruling underscores the practical application of avoiding *tashabbuh* (resemblance to idols) in daily worship spaces.
